solution.visualShortcut: Multiply each row first, combine subtotals, then apply the two percentages in order.
solution.explanation: Read the values from the chart and apply the stated operation. Formula: (Σ quantity × unit price) × (1 − discount ÷ 100) × (1 + tax ÷ 100). Final cost: after discount × (1 + tax ÷ 100); substitute 185.6 × (1 + 10 ÷ 100) = 204 EUR; rounded to nearest whole number. Final result: 204 EUR (rounded to nearest whole number where needed). passage.title: Managing an urgent translation queue
passage.text:
The Commission's translation unit schedules urgent requests in a shared queue. Requests marked urgent are reviewed by a coordinator before translators are assigned.

In June, 42 urgent requests entered the queue; 35 were assigned within two working days. The remainder waited for a specialist language pair.

The unit introduced a daily capacity cap of 18 assignments to protect quality. The cap applies to all requests, not only urgent ones.

passage.title: What the river sensors can show
passage.text:
The regional environment agency installed sensors at three river gauges in May. Each sensor records water level every 15 minutes and sends the readings to a central dashboard.

During the summer drought, the level at the Willow gauge stayed below the agency's alert threshold for nine days. Staff reviewed an alert before issuing any public bulletin.

Heavy rain in September produced two alerts in three days, but neither led to a closure because the water level receded within four hours. The sensors report current levels; they do not predict rainfall.

passage.title: The archive's first digitisation phase
passage.text:
The city archive prioritised maps dated before 1950 for its first digitisation phase. Each map is catalogued before scanning, and a quality check is completed before a public access copy is posted.

In May, the team scanned 320 maps. Volunteers transcribed handwritten labels for 90 of those maps; the volunteers did not operate the scanners.

The project creates digital access copies while the original maps remain in the archive reading room.

passage.title: A shorter visit to the permit office
passage.text:
To reduce waiting time, the North District permit office introduced an online pre-check in April. Applicants may upload forms before visiting, but an officer still verifies original identity documents at the appointment.

During the first six weeks, average counter time fell from 18 minutes to 11 minutes. The office handled 14% more applications than in the same period last year.

The office did not extend opening hours; it reassigned two clerks from filing to pre-checks.

passage.title: The archive's first digitisation phase
passage.text:
The city archive prioritised maps dated before 1950 for its first digitisation phase. Each map is catalogued before scanning, and a quality check is completed before a public access copy is posted.

In May, the team scanned 320 maps. Volunteers transcribed handwritten labels for 90 of those maps; the volunteers did not operate the scanners.

The project creates digital access copies while the original maps remain in the archive reading room.

passage.title: Managing an urgent translation queue
passage.text:
The Commission's translation unit schedules urgent requests in a shared queue. Requests marked urgent are reviewed by a coordinator before translators are assigned.

In June, 42 urgent requests entered the queue; 35 were assigned within two working days. The remainder waited for a specialist language pair.

The unit introduced a daily capacity cap of 18 assignments to protect quality. The cap applies to all requests, not only urgent ones.

passage.title: What the river sensors can show
passage.text:
The regional environment agency installed sensors at three river gauges in May. Each sensor records water level every 15 minutes and sends the readings to a central dashboard.

During the summer drought, the level at the Willow gauge stayed below the agency's alert threshold for nine days. Staff reviewed an alert before issuing any public bulletin.

Heavy rain in September produced two alerts in three days, but neither led to a closure because the water level receded within four hours. The sensors report current levels; they do not predict rainfall.

passage.title: The archive's first digitisation phase
passage.text:
The city archive prioritised maps dated before 1950 for its first digitisation phase. Each map is catalogued before scanning, and a quality check is completed before a public access copy is posted.

In May, the team scanned 320 maps. Volunteers transcribed handwritten labels for 90 of those maps; the volunteers did not operate the scanners.

The project creates digital access copies while the original maps remain in the archive reading room.

passage.title: A shorter visit to the permit office
passage.text:
To reduce waiting time, the North District permit office introduced an online pre-check in April. Applicants may upload forms before visiting, but an officer still verifies original identity documents at the appointment.

passage.title: The archive's first digitisation phase
passage.text:
The city archive prioritised maps dated before 1950 for its first digitisation phase. Each map is catalogued before scanning, and a quality check is completed before a public access copy is posted.

In May, the team scanned 320 maps. Volunteers transcribed handwritten labels for 90 of those maps; the volunteers did not operate the scanners.

The project creates digital access copies while the original maps remain in the archive reading room.

passage.title: Managing an urgent translation queue
passage.text:
The Commission's translation unit schedules urgent requests in a shared queue. Requests marked urgent are reviewed by a coordinator before translators are assigned.

In June, 42 urgent requests entered the queue; 35 were assigned within two working days. The remainder waited for a specialist language pair.

The unit introduced a daily capacity cap of 18 assignments to protect quality. The cap applies to all requests, not only urgent ones.

passage.title: What the river sensors can show
passage.text:
The regional environment agency installed sensors at three river gauges in May. Each sensor records water level every 15 minutes and sends the readings to a central dashboard.

During the summer drought, the level at the Willow gauge stayed below the agency's alert threshold for nine days. Staff reviewed an alert before issuing any public bulletin.

Heavy rain in September produced two alerts in three days, but neither led to a closure because the water level receded within four hours. The sensors report current levels; they do not predict rainfall.

passage.title: The archive's first digitisation phase
passage.text:
The city archive prioritised maps dated before 1950 for its first digitisation phase. Each map is catalogued before scanning, and a quality check is completed before a public access copy is posted.

In May, the team scanned 320 maps. Volunteers transcribed handwritten labels for 90 of those maps; the volunteers did not operate the scanners.

The project creates digital access copies while the original maps remain in the archive reading room.

To reduce waiting time, the North District permit office introduced an online pre-check in April. Applicants may upload forms before visiting, but an officer still verifies original identity documents at the appointment.

During the first six weeks, average counter time fell from 18 minutes to 11 minutes. The office handled 14% more applications than in the same period last year.

The office did not extend opening hours; it reassigned two clerks from filing to pre-checks.

passage.title: The archive's first digitisation phase
passage.text:
The city archive prioritised maps dated before 1950 for its first digitisation phase. Each map is catalogued before scanning, and a quality check is completed before a public access copy is posted.

In May, the team scanned 320 maps. Volunteers transcribed handwritten labels for 90 of those maps; the volunteers did not operate the scanners.

The project creates digital access copies while the original maps remain in the archive reading room.

solution.ruleText: rotate by 90° and move by (0, 0.1)
solution.explanation: The rule is applied in two directions: Rows rotate by 90°; columns move by (0, 0.1). Reading across each row and down each column gives the same local/global pattern. The missing bottom-right figure must therefore apply both changes. Option D is correct because it applies rotate by 90° and move by (0, 0.1). Other options omit one change or use a plausible wrong direction, rotation, fill, or element count.

passage.title: Managing an urgent translation queue
passage.text:
The Commission's translation unit schedules urgent requests in a shared queue. Requests marked urgent are reviewed by a coordinator before translators are assigned.

In June, 42 urgent requests entered the queue; 35 were assigned within two working days. The remainder waited for a specialist language pair.

The unit introduced a daily capacity cap of 18 assignments to protect quality. The cap applies to all requests, not only urgent ones.

passage.title: What the river sensors can show
passage.text:
The regional environment agency installed sensors at three river gauges in May. Each sensor records water level every 15 minutes and sends the readings to a central dashboard.

During the summer drought, the level at the Willow gauge stayed below the agency's alert threshold for nine days. Staff reviewed an alert before issuing any public bulletin.

Heavy rain in September produced two alerts in three days, but neither led to a closure because the water level receded within four hours. The sensors report current levels; they do not predict rainfall.

passage.title: The archive's first digitisation phase
passage.text:
The city archive prioritised maps dated before 1950 for its first digitisation phase. Each map is catalogued before scanning, and a quality check is completed before a public access copy is posted.

In May, the team scanned 320 maps. Volunteers transcribed handwritten labels for 90 of those maps; the volunteers did not operate the scanners.

The project creates digital access copies while the original maps remain in the archive reading room.

passage.title: A shorter visit to the permit office
passage.text:
To reduce waiting time, the North District permit office introduced an online pre-check in April. Applicants may upload forms before visiting, but an officer still verifies original identity documents at the appointment.

During the first six weeks, average counter time fell from 18 minutes to 11 minutes. The office handled 14% more applications than in the same period last year.

The office did not extend opening hours; it reassigned two clerks from filing to pre-checks.

passage.title: The archive's first digitisation phase
passage.text:
The city archive prioritised maps dated before 1950 for its first digitisation phase. Each map is catalogued before scanning, and a quality check is completed before a public access copy is posted.

In May, the team scanned 320 maps. Volunteers transcribed handwritten labels for 90 of those maps; the volunteers did not operate the scanners.

The project creates digital access copies while the original maps remain in the archive reading room.

Final cost: after discount × (1 + tax ÷ 100); substitute 185.6 × (1 + 10 ÷ 100) = 204.16 EUR; rounded to 2 decimal places. Final result: 204.16 EUR (rounded to 2 decimal places where needed). passage.title: Managing an urgent translation queue
passage.text:
The Commission's translation unit schedules urgent requests in a shared queue. Requests marked urgent are reviewed by a coordinator before translators are assigned.

In June, 42 urgent requests entered the queue; 35 were assigned within two working days. The remainder waited for a specialist language pair.

The unit introduced a daily capacity cap of 18 assignments to protect quality. The cap applies to all requests, not only urgent ones.

passage.title: What the river sensors can show
passage.text:
The regional environment agency installed sensors at three river gauges in May. Each sensor records water level every 15 minutes and sends the readings to a central dashboard.

During the summer drought, the level at the Willow gauge stayed below the agency's alert threshold for nine days. Staff reviewed an alert before issuing any public bulletin.

Heavy rain in September produced two alerts in three days, but neither led to a closure because the water level receded within four hours. The sensors report current levels; they do not predict rainfall.

passage.title: The archive's first digitisation phase
passage.text:
The city archive prioritised maps dated before 1950 for its first digitisation phase. Each map is catalogued before scanning, and a quality check is completed before a public access copy is posted.

In May, the team scanned 320 maps. Volunteers transcribed handwritten labels for 90 of those maps; the volunteers did not operate the scanners.

The project creates digital access copies while the original maps remain in the archive reading room.

solution.explanation: The rule is applied in two directions: Rows rotate by 90° and move by (0.07, 0.04); columns reflect across the vertical axis and change colour. Reading across each row and down each column gives the same local/global pattern. The missing bottom-right figure must therefore apply both changes. Option D is correct because it applies rotate by 90° and move by (0.07, 0.04) and reflect across the vertical axis and change colour. Other options omit one change or use a plausible wrong direction, rotation, fill, or element count.

passage.title: A shorter visit to the permit office
passage.text:
To reduce waiting time, the North District permit office introduced an online pre-check in April. Applicants may upload forms before visiting, but an officer still verifies original identity documents at the appointment.

During the first six weeks, average counter time fell from 18 minutes to 11 minutes. The office handled 14% more applications than in the same period last year.

The office did not extend opening hours; it reassigned two clerks from filing to pre-checks.

passage.title: The archive's first digitisation phase
passage.text:
The city archive prioritised maps dated before 1950 for its first digitisation phase. Each map is catalogued before scanning, and a quality check is completed before a public access copy is posted.

In May, the team scanned 320 maps. Volunteers transcribed handwritten labels for 90 of those maps; the volunteers did not operate the scanners.

The project creates digital access copies while the original maps remain in the archive reading room.

solution.explanation: The rule is applied in two directions: Rows rotate by 90° and move by (0.07, 0.04); columns reflect across the vertical axis and change colour. Reading across each row and down each column gives the same local/global pattern. The missing bottom-right figure must therefore apply both changes. Option D is correct because it applies rotate by 90° and move by (0.07, 0.04) and reflect across the vertical axis and change colour. Other options omit one change or use a plausible wrong direction, rotation, fill, or element count.

passage.title: Managing an urgent translation queue
passage.text:
The Commission's translation unit schedules urgent requests in a shared queue. Requests marked urgent are reviewed by a coordinator before translators are assigned.

In June, 42 urgent requests entered the queue; 35 were assigned within two working days. The remainder waited for a specialist language pair.

The unit introduced a daily capacity cap of 18 assignments to protect quality. The cap applies to all requests, not only urgent ones.

passage.title: What the river sensors can show
passage.text:
The regional environment agency installed sensors at three river gauges in May. Each sensor records water level every 15 minutes and sends the readings to a central dashboard.

During the summer drought, the level at the Willow gauge stayed below the agency's alert threshold for nine days. Staff reviewed an alert before issuing any public bulletin.

passage.title: The archive's first digitisation phase
passage.text:
The city archive prioritised maps dated before 1950 for its first digitisation phase. Each map is catalogued before scanning, and a quality check is completed before a public access copy is posted.

In May, the team scanned 320 maps. Volunteers transcribed handwritten labels for 90 of those maps; the volunteers did not operate the scanners.

The project creates digital access copies while the original maps remain in the archive reading room.

passage.title: A shorter visit to the permit office
passage.text:
To reduce waiting time, the North District permit office introduced an online pre-check in April. Applicants may upload forms before visiting, but an officer still verifies original identity documents at the appointment.

During the first six weeks, average counter time fell from 18 minutes to 11 minutes. The office handled 14% more applications than in the same period last year.

The office did not extend opening hours; it reassigned two clerks from filing to pre-checks.

passage.title: The archive's first digitisation phase
passage.text:
The city archive prioritised maps dated before 1950 for its first digitisation phase. Each map is catalogued before scanning, and a quality check is completed before a public access copy is posted.

In May, the team scanned 320 maps. Volunteers transcribed handwritten labels for 90 of those maps; the volunteers did not operate the scanners.

The project creates digital access copies while the original maps remain in the archive reading room.

In May, the team scanned 320 maps. Volunteers transcribed handwritten labels for 90 of those maps; the volunteers did not operate the scanners.

The project creates digital access copies while the original maps remain in the archive reading room.
